Debt is operating raw material for a bank, so an enterprise-value multiple would measure the wrong thing
Residual income qualified by NIM, asset quality and capital

dpsDeclared.note: dataset schema v1 carries no dividend declaration record; supply one to corroborate the cash-flow figure

reconciliation.reason: NO_DECLARATION_RECORD: no dividend declaration is available, so the two sources cannot be compared

factors.statement: Banking earnings are set inside a regulatory framework, so a rule change re-prices the business independently of operating performance.

confidence.formula: combined = 0.6 × dataConfidence + 0.4 × modelConfidence, then multiplied by each cap factor (ADEQUACY_PARTIAL 0.85, ADEQUACY_INSUFFICIENT 0.6, STALE_DATA 0.9, DILUTION_PROXY 0.98, DIVIDEND_SOURCE_CONFLICT 0.95, HIGH_METHOD_DISAGREEMENT 0.85), rounded to 4 dp

sectorReferenceView.note: This block is a sector reference, not an identity and not an input to the assessment. It is displayed separately and cannot drive any valuation, moat, dividend or risk field.

dividend sources reconciled with status NOT_COMPARABLE

limitations: Dilutive potential shares (ESOP, convertibles) are not present in dataset schema v1, so the diluted count is the EPS-implied count and carries the DILUTION_PROXY cap.

Net debt subtracts cash and cash equivalents plus liquid investments only; restricted balances, margin money and regulatory balances are excluded from available cash by construction (R-4.1 / Schedule III). Dataset schema v1 carries no restricted-balance line item, so the component is published as NOT_COMPUTABLE rather than as a zero.
The corporate-action table carries no dividend declaration record in dataset schema v1, so R-15 corroboration is unavailable for this assessment.
Net debt could not be derived (NOT_REPORTED), so every enterprise-value method is withheld rather than run on a partial bridge.
Assessment only: no persistence, no transport and no UI are part of IID-2 (IID-3 and IID-6 own those).
